title: A missed deadline is reaped
text: The transition `answer` has `deadline(500)`: if the executor falls behind and `answer` is still armed 505 ms after it was armed (500 ms plus the default 5 ms tolerance), the executor reaps it instead of firing it late. A reaped transition keeps its input tokens and stays quiet until a firing writes one of its places, here `reopen` at 2000 ms.

steps.text: A blocking action held the executor past 505 ms, so `answer` was reaped: no firing, a `TransitionTimedOut` event, and the `ticket` stays. The transition `reopen` has `exact(2000)`, which is never reaped: it fires at 2000 ms, or as soon after as it can.
The transition `reopen` wrote `ticket`, so `answer` is armed again with a fresh clock and fires within its deadline, taking the older ticket first.

It fires again for the second ticket. Had the executor stayed behind, `answer` would rest reaped with a ticket left, which is why verification counts a marking that enables only reapable transitions as quiescent.
